Longshot Wolf's Scroll of Proof

Every call LongShotWolf made on the record — the spread calls and the three-minute reads — timestamped when it fired, then graded against what the tape actually did. The misses are on this page, right next to the hits. Nobody else in this market publishes theirs.

Signal rooms charge $50–$225 a month on claimed win rates. This page is the audit before anyone pays a cent: 2,478 entries — 1,451 graded calls: the 804 spread calls of Weeks 1–3, graded mechanically under rules locked on Oct 24, 2026 and never loosened since, and 647 three-minute calls, every one on Litecoin, backfilled on his Nov 15, 2026 ruling and graded under his mechanical 3M doctrine — plus 1,027 Four Points level touches, every one a DIRECT HIT, each printed in full below. How every row is graded

Locked Oct 24, 2026. Never loosened retroactively — Week 1 keeps its original grades, untouched.

The window

Each call is graded from the minute it fired to the close of the 6H candle it was made in, against Bitunix futures tape. The call was posted publicly first — in Discord #spread-reading, the army spread rooms, or Kick chat — so the timestamp exists outside this page.

The bands

BTC: cycle $300 · a move $500 · better $800 · big big $1,000. LTC: cycle $0.60 · big $1.00. ETH: provisional $15 / $30. A band call is a HIT when price runs the floor in the called direction; a MISS when it first travels more than half the floor the other way; in between is PARTIAL — direction right, size short.

The 20% range rule

From Week 2, by his teaching: a call is a range, not a point — "you can never really call a direct hit on any coin, by the way they move." A run reaching 80% of the floor grades HIT; 50–80% grades SHORT. Every row shows the actual run next to the call, with a closeness stamp — within 10% / 15% / 20% of the call, or past the number.

What is not on this sheet: Field Radar readings (scheduled system reports, not his calls), battlefield board flips, and dictated ad reads. The sheet holds his calls only — that's what makes it proof of the reader, not of the machinery around him. One exception, by his own word on Nov 22, 2026: the two standing laws in the next section are printed on this page in full — they are house law, not calls, they carry no grade, and they change no grade, row, or total above or below.

Standing laws — printed in full

Added Nov 22, 2026, on the Warlord's direct order — put in with full description, everywhere, so the house remembers them too.

The Leverage Pullback — Down 50%, Back to 5x

His words, locked Nov 22, 2026: “Once it go down 50% they should pull it back to five x.” That locked wording completes his order from earlier the same day — that when a trade goes down on a bot, the bot has got to know to push the lever — the leverage — back.

What it means, in full — For every trading bot on the paper game, the moment an OPEN position is down 50% — the position's percentage loss figured the game book's own way, the position's profit-and-loss against the fixed 10,000-sat margin — the bot pulls THAT trade's leverage back to 5x. The trigger is the −50% line itself, not a sat count: this locked rule supersedes the morning's −3,000-sat framing. It is the same trade that gets pulled back — the position stays open, nothing is closed, and it is not a setting saved up for the next entry.

How it runs — The pullback fires once per position. The accrued profit-and-loss is carried with the trade, the reference is re-set, and the liquidation price is recomputed — the loss already taken stays taken, now carried at the new 5x leverage. If the game refuses the adjustment, the rule does not force it: it stands ready and tries again on the next cycle. Every firing is written into the bot's ledger as a LEVERAGE_PULLBACK event — the coin, the side, the old leverage, the new leverage of 5x, and the percentage down.

What it does not touch — It is not an exit. Entry logic, the 500-sat take-profit, the +100-sat profit floor, and the Four Points exits all stand exactly as they stood, with their order of precedence untouched. The rule was wired into the shared bot engine and verified on Nov 22, 2026 — from that day forward it stands armed on every bot trade, and it stands printed here, in full, by his order.

Handed-Out Links Carry Full Commands

His scope, read back to him on Nov 22, 2026 and confirmed — “Correct.” In his own words: “That we give to somebody, not just every link. The ones that we give out.”

What it means, in full — For now, anybody the house gives a link to gets the full game through it: any link or lane the house HANDS to somebody carries full command and full access to all commands to play the paper game — open a trade at the leverage they choose, close, push the lever up, pull the lever down, rank, and every other command the game itself speaks. A handed-out link never carries a cut-down set.

The fence, stated plain — This rule covers only the links the house gives out, to the people it gives them to. It does not cover every link: public doors, view copies, and links that are simply posted or watched are untouched by it, and keep exactly the access they already carry.

Why it stands here — He ordered it written into the DNA and onto this Proof Page so the house can remember it too — a standing rule, printed where it can be found again. Its first application came the same night, Nov 22, 2026: Astra's paper-game lane, which had stood open-and-close only, was opened to full commands — the leverage adjustment and the full game-command passthrough included — proven live from the public side, with her open trade left exactly as she had it.

Four Points

Every recorded touch of a marked Four Points level — each one a DIRECT HIT, each printed in full, times in New York.

Four Points is the level system riding beside the spread record: for each of the big 3, on the 6H, day, week and month candles, the system marks four levels — Point 1, the end of candle away from the wick; Point 2; Point 3, where candle and wick meet; and Point 4. When live price reaches a marked level, the watcher fires at that moment and posts the hit to the channel. On the Warlord's order (Nov 13, 2026), every one of those hits is on this page — the whole record, back to the first hit the watcher ever logged — each graded DIRECT HIT and counted in the combined record above, and each carrying its full description of what it did. New hits flow onto this page on every refresh from here on.

His 3-minute slowing and pushing reads — every one graded against the 3M tape, times in New York. All 647 on Litecoin.

ALL 647 ON LITECOIN — HIS COIN, AND THE COIN THE 3M READ WAS TAUGHT ON
What happened — every count in this box is a call he actually made: 645 typed in his own Kick chat, and 2 spoken on the Nov 15, 2026 voice call and marked spoken on their rows — each one graded mechanically over the two 3-minute candles after it, under the doctrine set out in the method below. The misses are printed at the same size as the hits — all 479 of them.

The record runs from the first call on Oct 25, 2026 to the latest on Nov 24, 2026 — the two spoken calls, M3-617 and M3-618, sit in the Nov 15 box, their spoken-call disclosure carried in their own descriptions. Method & disclosures — from the three-minute ledger

BACKGRADE ORDER (Nov 15, 2026): the Warlord ruled 'Go back as far as you can go back and put them on the proof page.' This ledger grades his 3-minute slowing/pushing calls as real graded entries. It supersedes the house's older convention, under which his typed 'slowing on the 3 min' reads were disclosed in candle notes as proximity reads and NOT graded; that convention was the house's, and the record now follows his ruling.

REACH: the earliest call graded here is at 2026-10-25T05:21:11Z — the first 3M read in the surviving Kick chat capture. The capture itself begins 2026-10-25 05:20Z; before that the trail genuinely ends — no earlier call is entered, because none survives to grade.

SOURCES in his order of trust: (a) his own free-typed Kick chat lines (pasted house posts never count) — 641 entries; (b) 3M reads quoted verbatim in the old candle notes, each cited to its note in its source field — the notes were swept and every 3M read they quote was already in the chat capture, so this source adds no separate entries — nothing was double-counted. (c) the two LTC calls he SPOKE on the Nov 15, 2026 voice call, marked spoken and confirmed against the shared engine at the time — 2 entries. A house record showing only a bot's read, with no trace of his call, never becomes his graded call.

COIN: his typed 3M lines name no coin; all are graded against Litecoin — his coin, the coin the 3M doctrine was taught on, and the standing house rule where no coin is named. Every such description says so plainly.

GRADING (his mechanical doctrine, exactly as the 3-minute gate runs it): over the two 3M Heikin-Ashi candles after the call candle — SLOWING is a HIT only when both following candles are littler than the call candle AND no fresh ground is made in the called direction (fresh ground forces PUSHING regardless of candle size); otherwise a MISS. PUSHING is a HIT when fresh ground is made, a MISS when the slowing gate fires instead, UNGRADED when the tape settles neither. Gappy or missing tape is UNGRADED with the reason stated — a grade is never guessed.

The grading recipe is saved at grade_3m_backfill.py beside this ledger; the fetched Bitunix tape is cached at tape_ltc_3m_cache.json so every grade can be re-derived.

The misses that prove the rules

Strict-rule misses keep their footnotes. They are never re-graded.

Row W2-01 — LTC, Oct 24, 5:04 AM MISS

Called a −$0.92 CYCLE down at $56.22. Price then fell $1.16 — 193% of the cycle number. Direction right, size right — but before the run, price bounced +$0.32, two cents past the $0.30 half-floor line. Adverse-first is a miss under the locked rules. It sits on the sheet as a miss, footnote and all.

Row B07 — BTC, Week 1 MISS

Price first pulled back $349.40, crossing the $250 half-floor — then traveled $1,293.90 favorable and the spread peaked at +1,999 that candle. The forward-path rule grades the pullback-first sequence a miss. Disclosed in full on the row, never quietly flipped to a hit.

Row B23 — ETH, Week 1 MISS

ETH first bounced $18.37 — over the $15 half-floor — then fell $41.05. The drop came; it came after the adverse line was crossed. Miss, by the mechanical rule. A record that only counts the convenient rows isn't a record. This one counts the rule.

The comeback misses

Went the other way first — past the grading floor — then came back and ran for him. All 44 still grade MISS.
44

of the 230 misses in the week ledgers first went against the call — then came back and ran in his favor anyway.

The biggest: W3-03 (BTC, Nov 4) — price traveled $331.9 against the call, past the $250 half-floor, then ran $2,878.5 for him — 507% of the call number. The closest: W2-28 broke adverse-first by six cents, then ran 194% of the number. Both read MISS on this sheet, and both always will.

Split of the 44: Week 1 · 2 — Week 2 · 10 — Week 3 · 32. By coin: BTC 14 · ETH 16 · LTC 14.

Read this plainly: the miss stands. Under the strict rule locked Oct 24, a call that crosses the grading floor the wrong way first is a MISS — even when price later comes all the way back and runs past the number. No grade on this page changes because of this section, and no total moves: these 44 sit inside the 230 misses of the three week ledgers — the calls book as a whole, the 647 three-minute calls counted in, now reads 1,439 calls — 539 HIT · 11 PARTIAL · 12 SHORT · 709 MISS · 168 UNGRADED. This section exists so the full picture is on the record: how far each one went against him first, and how far it then ran for him.

How the 44 were counted — mechanically, from the three ledgers, never by hand: a row graded MISS whose ledger note records the adverse-first strict-rule pattern (price crossed the half-floor against the call before the run) and whose forward run then reached at least 80% of the call number — the hit line under the 20% range rule (the ledgers' pct_of_call field; Week 1 rows carry no pct field, so theirs is measured against the band floor). 90 other misses carry an adverse-first note too, but the run back stopped short of the line — they are plain misses, and they are not in this table.

Sources & method. Grades computed mechanically from Bitunix futures klines under the rules locked Oct 24, 2026; Week 1 ledger (94 rows, Oct 18–24), Week 2 ledger (139 rows, graded through Candle 22, Oct 29), Week 3 ledger (571 rows, graded through Candle 136, Nov 27), the Four Points ledger (1,027 direct hits, Nov 9–27, from the watcher's own hit log), and the three-minute ledger (647 graded calls, Oct 25 – Nov 24, backfilled Nov 15, 2026 on the Warlord's ruling) are the underlying records, and every row above is reproduced from them — call text, timestamp (Phoenix for the week ledgers, except rows W3-115 and W3-116, printed in New York time as called; New York time for the Four Points and three-minute rows), and grade unchanged. Early Week 1 windows were graded at 1h/15m granularity where 3m history doesn't reach; that is noted on the affected rows in the ledger. Log-vs-tape disagreements found during grading are flagged on their rows, not smoothed over. This page is a snapshot built Nov 27, 2026 — the live record keeps grading at every 6H candle close.

Standing laws, restated at the foot of the record. The Leverage Pullback — when an open bot position on the paper game goes down 50% (figured against the fixed 10,000-sat margin), that same trade's leverage is pulled back to 5x and the position stays open; it is not a close and not an exit. Handed-Out Links Carry Full Commands — a link or lane the house hands to somebody carries full command and full access to all commands to play the game — open at their chosen leverage, close, push the lever up or pull it down, rank, every command the game speaks — and this covers only the links the house gives out, never every link; public doors and view copies are untouched by it. Both laws were ordered printed in full on this page on Nov 22, 2026, and stand in full in the standing-laws section above. They are house law, not graded calls: they add no entries to the sheet and move no total on it.

Not financial advice. This page documents a public track record; past graded calls do not guarantee future ones — the misses above are the reminder.
